title: About 20,000 People, One 3.1-Mile Table and a New World Record in Romania
summary:
How long can a table be? In Bucharest, Romania, the answer is 3.1 miles.

On September 12, 2026, about 20,000 people gathered for a community meal at the "Uniting Table." Stretching 3.1 miles (4.99 km), it set a new Guinness World Record for the longest table made from recycled materials.

But the record was only part of the goal. The event, organized by the nonprofit Bloom The World, was also a fundraiser. It raised more than $110,000 for Romania's first psychiatric hospital for children. Currently, children in Bucharest who need mental health care are treated in an outdated facility with large, crowded wards that lack basic privacy. The new hospital is set to open in 2027 and will provide care for children with conditions such as depression, autism and ADHD.

This was the second time Bloom achieved this record. In 2025, the nonprofit brought together 10,000 people around a 1.7-mile (2.7 km) table made from recycled materials. That event was held in Alba Iulia, Romania, and focused on bringing people together and raising environmental awareness.

The story doesn't end when the meal does. Bloom plans to recycle the materials from its latest record-breaking table again. This time, they will be used to make children's furniture.
why_it_matters: The story shows how a record-setting event can also raise money for a cause and reuse materials. It also points to a need for better mental health care for children in Bucharest.
